newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: WOLTERS SAYS IT INTERESTED IN LIAISONS.
newsitem.headline: WOLTERS SAYS IT INTERESTED IN LIAISONS.

text.p: Dutch publisher Wolters Kluwer NV said on Thursday it was holding talks with a view to a possible takeover of French publisher Groupe Liaisons.
"We are indeed in talks with Groupe Liaisons, just as we are in talks with so many others," a Wolters spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman was commenting on a report in today's edtion of Le Monde saying that Wolters Kluwer was about to buy the provately-owned Groupe Liaisons.
Le Monde said Groupe Liaisons was a publisher of some 50 business and professional titles with turnover of 363 million francs and net profit of 8.4 million francs in 1995.
The newspaper said several companies had been rumoured as possible buyers of Liaisons, including Pearson, Bertelsmann, Reed Elsevier and CEP Communication.
But it quoted the 76-year-old founder of Liaisons, Patrice-Aristide Blank, as saying that he preferred Wolters Kluwer as its activities complemented those of Liaisons.
The French group's best known titles include Liaisons Sociales, Le Moniteur des Pharmacies, l'Officiel des Transporteurs and Echo de la Presse et de la Publicite.

Wolters Kluwer is a business, legal, tax, medical and scientific publisher with annual sales of some 4.2 billion guilders. In 1995 France accounted for seven percent of the Dutch group's worldwide sales and operating profits.
